new.md:
Creates a new `GtkTextTagTable`.

The table contains no tags by default.

doc.md:
Collects the tags in a `GtkTextBuffer`.

You may wish to begin by reading the
[text widget conceptual overview](section-text-widget.html),
which gives an overview of all the objects and data types
related to the text widget and how they work together.

# GtkTextTagTables as GtkBuildable

The `GtkTextTagTable` implementation of the `GtkBuildable` interface
supports adding tags by specifying “tag” as the “type” attribute
of a `<child>` element.

An example of a UI definition fragment specifying tags:
```xml
<object class="GtkTextTagTable">
 <child type="tag">
   <object class="GtkTextTag"/>
 </child>
</object>
```

add.brief: Add a tag to the table.
add.md:
Add a tag to the table.

The tag is assigned the highest priority in the table.

`tag` must not be in a tag table already, and may not have
the same name as an already-added tag.

foreach.brief: Calls `func` on each tag in `table`, with user data `data`.
foreach.md:
Calls `func` on each tag in `table`, with user data `data`.

Note that the table may not be modified while iterating
over it (you can’t add/remove tags).

get_size.brief: Returns the size of the table (number of tags)
get_size.md: Returns the size of the table (number of tags)

remove.brief: Remove a tag from the table.
remove.md:
Remove a tag from the table.

If a `GtkTextBuffer` has `table` as its tag table, the tag is
removed from the buffer. The table’s reference to the tag is
removed, so the tag will end up destroyed if you don’t have
a reference to it.

tag-added.brief: Emitted every time a new tag is added in the `GtkTextTagTable`.
tag-added.md: Emitted every time a new tag is added in the `GtkTextTagTable`.

tag-changed.brief: Emitted every time a tag in the `GtkTextTagTable` changes.
tag-changed.md: Emitted every time a tag in the `GtkTextTagTable` changes.

tag-removed.brief: Emitted every time a tag is removed from the `GtkTextTagTable`.
tag-removed.md:
Emitted every time a tag is removed from the `GtkTextTagTable`.

The `tag` is still valid by the time the signal is emitted, but
it is not associated with a tag table any more.
